newsitem.title: EGYPT: Jihad group threatens to avenge killing of leader.
newsitem.headline: Jihad group threatens to avenge killing of leader.

text.p: The head of the Palestinian militant group Islamic Jihad has said that heavy security in Israel hampered attempts to avenge the killing of its leader a year ago, but it was just waiting for the right moment.
Ramadan Abdallah Shallah told the weekly magazine al-Wasat in an interview made available on Thursday that the group would avenge the killing of Fathi Shqaqi in Malta on October 26, 1995.
"Israel has transformed Palestine into a barricade the likes of which we have never seen and naturally this delays our work and makes it difficult," Shallah said from his headquarters in Damascus.

"But Israelis have to know that Shqaqi is not just a passing name and we warn them that...his sceptre will rise at any time from any place in Palestine," he added. "We're just waiting for the appropriate moment."
Israel went on high alert for fear of a possible suicide attack by the organisation to mark the anniversary. Shqaqi's killers were never caught but Palestinians blame Israel.
Palestinian police in the self-ruled Gaza Strip last month arrested dozens of Islamic Jihad members before the anniversary to pre-empt any attacks.
